ops.title: general-pack rm safety hook shipped 2026-07-16 (commit 8e32bb48, CHANGELOG 9.19.0) — outside-repo/glob>10/repo-root blocks, shared scratch predicate seam, adversarial-review hardening
ops.body:
The general-pack `deletions` hook (blocks Bash `rm` outside git/jj repos, globs matching >10 files, and repo-root deletion) shipped 2026-07-16 as commit 8e32bb48, CHANGELOG **9.19.0** — 9.17.0/9.18.0 were burned by concurrent releases mid-work (the [[concurrent-release-race-protocol]] strikes again; PyPI-check at tag time caught it before push). Release tag still pending.

Key seams and decisions (full threat model in cc-notes doc 54548bc9):
- `captain_hook/util/scratch.is_scratch_path` is the ONE scratch predicate — shared by `scratch_writes.py` and the rm guard, and the future seam for cc-transcript's session-scratchpad locator (uncommitted there as of 2026-07-16; its paths resolve under TEMP_ROOTS already). Never fork a second definition.
- Glob rule is deliberately NOT scratch-exempt; `WALK_BUDGET=20_000` `**` scans fail closed; leaf symlinks never dereferenced; `$`-token rm targets fail closed while unresolvable `cd` fails open (both deliberate, tested).
- Wrapper-arity bypasses (`env -u HOME rm`, `sudo -u root rm`, `timeout 5s rm`) are a cc-transcript `Command.unwrapped` gap — backlog task d026e9cd; delete the hook's local dequote/unescape normalization when it lands.

Process lesson: the codex-wrapper agent lost its process 3× in one run (implementer's codex died silently mid-run; both reviewers' exit-Monitors never fired and completed replies sat 5h unread). Recovery that works: read `codex-ask` scratch dirs directly (`/var/folders/.../T/codex-ask.*/codex-r-*` or the `-s` dir from `ps`), judge liveness by process tree, completion by non-empty reply file. See [[codex-wrapper-must-own-process]]; papercut filed 2026-07-16.
